why: Kilo reconciled AUDJPY by audit3's own fields (beta_dominant, alpha_gate, recency). That settles whether the aggregate is alpha; it does not settle whether the two trade-level samples are the same trades. A pick-id join does.

join.method: pick id, then embedded timestamp, then symbol

finding: THREE DISJOINT POPULATIONS, not one contradictory population. P2 (n=24) and P3 (n=32) share ZERO pick ids and ZERO embedded timestamps, and their id spaces are structurally different (['1382', '1385', '1391', '1401', '1403', '1405'] vs ['consensus', 'kimi', 'multi']). P1 publishes no trade ids at all, so it cannot be joined by id. The 'conflict' Kilo reported between +0.576% and -2.45% was never a contradiction inside one dataset: it compares an aggregate over one set with trades from two other sets. Kilo's field-level conclusion (beta_dominant, alpha_gate false, recent_ok false) is the operative one and stands.
